title: Plasma bradykinin in angio-oedema
authors: Nussberger J, Cugno M, Amstutz C, Cicardi M, Pellacani A, Agostoni A
population: 22 patients with hereditary angio-oedema, 4 with acquired C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency, 1 hypertensive patient with captopril-associated angio-oedema and 22 healthy volunteers
funder: not read: the publisher page is not accessible and the PubMed abstract carries no funding statement.
result: With a specific assay (liquid-phase extraction, HPLC and radioimmunoassay), plasma bradykinin rose to two to twelve times the upper limit of normal during attacks of hereditary and acquired angio-oedema. In the single patient treated with captopril, plasma bradykinin was 47 fmol/ml during an acute attack and 3.2 fmol/ml in remission after withdrawal of the drug, against a geometric mean of 2.2 fmol/ml in healthy volunteers.
